title: What AI services can produce good sprite sheets
author: ElvenSlayer
selftext:
Heyo! 

Just want some 2D character spritesheets so was wondering if there's any ai services that have gotten good enough to generate good looking ones? 

Not for commercial use, just for a portfolio project.

comments.author: Skalion
comments.body:
Just tried Gemini pro and got a pretty good result for a 32x32 pixel character, including different animations. 

Very consistent with the character, but I would have to do some adjustments, but that would be just maybe an hour to have a whole sprite sheet

comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body: whatever you end up using just know you will have to clean it up in a pixel art program its not bad to but don't expect perfect results! I use all of them because some are better at other at different animations and items there really isn't a one shoe fits all solution that i know of

comments.author: RealAstropulse
comments.body:
If you're looking for pixel art, my company retro diffusion does it really well. Animations are still difficult but I've made some pretty solid ones.

https://i.redd.it/lolrayrj85cg1.gif

comments.author: Microtom_
comments.body: Make a very simple 3d model, animate frames if you want, then give your renders to nano banana pro, asking to make the image into pixel art.

replies.author: _strongest_avenger_
replies.body: Put shit in butt, wiggle it around a bit if you’d like, and then poop out crap from ass and ask it to be dookie doo.

replies.author: Touitoui
replies.body:
"Use a simple 3d model to make pixel art" is a technique that was used for Dead Cell (minus the AI part, it was a homebrew software that "pixelated" the image).  
  
I find the method really interresting (especially since the 3d model can even be reused to make different characters):  
[https://www.gamedeveloper.com/production/art-design-deep-dive-using-a-3d-pipeline-for-2d-animation-in-i-dead-cells-i-](https://www.gamedeveloper.com/production/art-design-deep-dive-using-a-3d-pipeline-for-2d-animation-in-i-dead-cells-i-)

comments.author: blackwidowink
comments.body: I highly recommend Autosprite.io. I’ve used them for several games now and they’re getting better and better.

comments.body: I would highly recommend Retro diffusion as well as AutoSprite, both are good in my workflow

comments.author: Straight-Tea-8564
comments.body: I created an application for my personal use. It follows a technique that works very well. First you generate an AI video using the character’s first frame, animating that frame with a green background behind it. After that you can remove the background and you end up with a smooth animation. I use Kling and some tools I built in JavaScript to remove the background and clean the remaining elements.

comments.body: [sprite.chat](http://sprite.chat) may be a good option. They've got a demo game to try sprites and sprite sheets. The service allows edits with conversations.
